terminal_record.title: Unverified Allegation: Hegseth Made Trump Loyalty a Promotion Requirement
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied claim that Hegseth made Trump loyalty a promotion requirement remains unverified; available sources do not establish such a rule.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth changed military promotion rules in March 2025 to prioritize loyalty to Donald Trump over merit. The packet does not establish that a directive or formal promotion rule was issued. A March 7 Hill opinion discussed whether the selection of Dan Caine could signal loyalty over competency; it concerned one appointment, not a general promotion requirement. This internal draft remains unpublished and unverified.
terminal_record.description_long: The supplied entry alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth changed military promotion rules in March 2025 so loyalty to Donald Trump outweighed merit, combat experience, and professional qualifications. The packet does not identify a directive, promotion instruction, or rule text establishing that requirement; March 1 is an approximate supplied date, not a verified implementation date. A supplied Department of Defense source note describes promotion decisions as merit-based, but the referenced pages were not independently re-extracted in the research packet, so that description is not treated as a verified quotation. A March 7, 2025 Hill opinion says the selection of retired Lt. Gen. Dan Caine could signal loyalty over competency-based advancement. The passage is commentary about one senior appointment and does not establish a general promotion-system change. The supplied entry also predicts officer departures and effects on military effectiveness and national security, but the packet provides no outcome evidence for those predictions. This is an internal, unpublished draft of the supplied allegation, not a finding that a loyalty test was enacted or that those harms occurred. Publication remains ineligible until a directive or credible report establishes the alleged rule and its scope.

terminal_record.title: Trump and Abe Golfed at Trump National in Florida During Abe’s 2017 Visit
terminal_record.description_short: The Feb. 11, 2017 public schedule lists Trump golfing with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter.
terminal_record.description_medium: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed him playing golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The supplied allegation that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded course in Japan is not confirmed by that schedule and remains unverified. This correction records the same visit’s documented golf outing without asserting a business pitch.
terminal_record.description_long: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed a round of golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The schedule is the evidence for the date, participants and venue of the outing. It places the golf game within Abe’s official U.S. visit; it does not record their conversation. The frozen description alleged that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded golf course in Japan and discussed his private golf business. The accessed schedule entry records the golf outing but does not describe what the two leaders said or showed each other. Because a missing mention does not disprove a private conversation, that part remains an allegation requiring a source that reports what was shown or discussed. This corrected draft retains the same February 2017 Abe visit and the golf outing documented by the public schedule. It narrows the event to what the source states and removes claims about a Japanese course proposal, business promotion, or ethics experts’ assessment. It does not imply the outing alone established wrongdoing or that the trip produced a business agreement. Keep the original allegation unpublished unless it can be tied to a contemporaneous credible report or documentary record.
